why_this_direction: The same FF20 warning precedes correct and wrong descents. Determine whether the subsequent layers transform comparable incoming computation differently, using actual naturally reached FF20 outputs, with all 43 subsequent merges in their execution order.
repeating_pattern_check: A fixed location in the transferred response landed after the decision. The new score is available at any prediction independently of future events. A global scalar hid local variation, and a score present on valid routes could misdirect weight updates. Save all local signed contrasts. Score each true pre-operation event and off-phase triggers separately.
hypothesis: Conditional on an FF20 landmark shared by correct and incorrect paths, the subsequent layer transformations distinguish failing computations and track actual observed weight repairs while remaining quiet on valid operations.
prediction: The combined rule should retain the thirteen known failing descents and avoid the five correct descents with the same warning. The known reordered failure should flag before its wrong operation. The 387→388 sign repair and two earlier weight-family repairs should move the score toward correct. The already-correct 175→189 transition should remain clear. A missing landmark at a control is recorded separately from the route score.
would_weaken_it: Missed wrong descents, false alarms on the five or other correct cases, an unspecific warning throughout good responses, a lost transfer-case warning, or a repair going in the wrong direction. A downstream score no better than its input alone does not establish new downstream information.

rules.donors: Use five correct and thirteen wrong responses that shared the two-event warning in the previously completed timing study. For each use the existing computationally registered donor row from the historical overlap. Do not use true choice timing to select donor rows. For a query exclude every case with the same initial energy and descent work. The temporal landmark uses the previous 28-donor FF20 direction and midpoint under the same energy exclusions. All examples including the previously reordered one are development evidence.
rules.context: Unit FF20 outgoing residual is the single entering context at the start of the downstream segment. Separately in each class find the nearest convex combination of eligible donor input directions. Carry those coefficients through all 43 recorded downstream merges of that prediction. Report distance to each convex set and use their squared-distance difference as input-only comparison. Also compare the unconditioned class means on the identical downstream features.
rules.score: At each subsequent merge compute squared turn-vector distance to the conditional successful transformation minus squared distance to the conditional failing transformation. Positive means closer to failing. Primary downstream score sums over every merge after FF20 at this event with equal weight. Report separate log-gain scores wherever captured; never tune their scale or use them for the primary decision. Report per-merge contributions and class weights at the relevant events. No empirical hyperparameter search.
rules.online: Every prediction has an FF20 locator score. A candidate event is the second or later in a consecutive positive stretch. Score all such events including off-phase and after the decision. Primary alarm is candidate and positive downstream score. Also score the last event before the verified descent action, even if the locator was quiet, for diagnosis only. Report counts gate, input-only, unconditioned, conditional and joint at that location, separately on the original five, thirteen and other ten. Record earlier plus later alarms across full histories. Native decisions from equations are evaluation annotations, never inputs to the candidate score.
rules.weight_controls: Score saved naturally generated 387 and 388; 175 and 189; the early, late-attention, late-FFN and late endpoints of the fitted swap; and the previously missed reordered problem. Controls exclude the fit or reordered energy group as appropriate. Compare signed values as well as flags. If separately archived controls require restored bytes, verify source checksums. Local extraction and archive retrieval only; no checkpoint creation or training under this declaration.

what_went_wrong_before: Earlier one-pair fitting reduced its objective while failing to transfer the descent. A signal that needs the arithmetic decision to choose the comparison event cannot act as the online locator. The original five and thirteen membership and historical donor registration were already examined.
status: Saved-data comparison prospectively specified after the landmark timing study.
rule: Locate recurrent FF20 warnings, then score downstream transformations at comparable FF20 outputs using the class-conditional rules below.

companion_registration.basis: Before generating any downstream class score, checking prior recorded rows revealed two of five valid donor anchors lie 32 and 33 events later than the event preceding the evaluated descent; all thirteen failing anchors and the other three valid anchors coincide. This asymmetry can confound a downstream comparison.
companion_registration.rule: Keep original registered analysis as primary. In a separate comparison choose the first double-positive event in each eligible donor full decode. Compute that donor locator from the previously registered 28-donor bank excluding both the outer query energy group and that donor energy group. A donor with no such event is unavailable. Keep the query gate, state, downstream score, planes and zero boundary unchanged. Report exact selected native rows, missing donors and their distance from the annotated event diagnostically. First warning can precede the physical operation.
